title: Ordinary condensed Galois descent for global derived sections
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure, $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology, and $X$ a qcqs $k$-scheme. Write $X^s=X\times_k k^s$. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring, $R_T=p_T^*R$, and use internal module categories and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for internal $R$-modules with the condensed $G$-action of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The equivariant geometric section functor sends an $R_X$-module $M$ to the condensed $R$-module whose sections at a profinite set $P$ are $\Gamma(X^s\times P,M|_{X^s\times P})$, with the action induced by the $k$-descent of $M$; $X^s\times P$ denotes the inverse limit of finite disjoint copies of $X^s$ along finite quotients of $P$. Denote its ordinary total right derived functor by $\mathcal K_R:D(R_X)\to D(\mathcal A_G(R))$. The equivariant module category is Grothendieck abelian; its invariant-submodule functor has the ordinary total right derived functor $R\Gamma_G$. Evaluation at the one-point profinite set, followed by forgetting scalars, is denoted $\operatorname{ev}_*$. It is exact on condensed modules.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of exact functors to $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$\delta_{R,M}:R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_* R\Gamma_G(\mathcal K_R(M)).$$
For a morphism $R\to R'$, an $R_X$-complex $M$, and an $R'_X$-complex $M'$, the isomorphisms commute with every morphism $M\to\operatorname{Res}M'$ and the corresponding geometric and invariant morphisms after scalar restriction. They are also compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles. The assertion is in the ordinary derived categories and does not replace derived internal-function bar terms by underived continuous cochains. No finite cohomological dimension of $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a:X\to s$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-profinite-galois-site] to replace sheaves on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by sheaves on $\mathbf{Prof}_G$. The subsite is dense with its induced topology and all sites are small in the chosen larger universe, so [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] applies. Denote a profinite test scheme by $T[P]$. In particular $\bar s[P]$ corresponds to the free profinite $G$-set $G\times P$ and $s[P]$ to the trivial $G$-set $P$.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9-4.1.10; restriction to the dense qcqs subsite

proof.text: The full subcategory of free objects $G\times P$ is dense in $\mathbf{Prof}_G$: $G\times S\to S$, $(g,x)\mapsto gx$, is an equivariant surjection for every profinite $G$-set $S$. Every equivariant map $G\times T\to G\times P$ uniquely has the form $(g,t)\mapsto(gb(t),f(t))$ for continuous $f:T\to P$ and $b:T\to G$, by evaluation at $(1,t)$. Composing $(f,b)$ and $(h,c)$ gives $(fh,c\,h^*b)$. A finite family of these maps is jointly surjective exactly when its family of maps $f$ is jointly surjective. Thus the free subsite is precisely the action site $C_G$ of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] again and that node's equivalence with internal actions. This gives an equivalence of topoi $E:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}$ with $(EF)(P)=F(\bar s[P])$. The action is pullback by right translation on the free $G$-factor. The composition formula above agrees with the action site's stated convention.

source.place: Example 4.1.10 and §4.3; elementary free-subsite calculation using the cited action-site equivalence

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ on $\mathbf{Prof}_G$, descent for the covering $G\times P\to P$ (with trivial action on $P$) identifies $F(P)$ with the sections of $(EF)(P)$ fixed after all profinite base changes. Indeed its kernel pair is $G\times G\times P$; the two restrictions are the identity and the action, so their equalizer is exactly that fixed-section subobject. The same formula is natural in $P$. By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], $p_{s*}F(P)=F(s[P])=F(P)$, whereas [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], applied with $H=1$ to the condensed ring $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ (whose internal modules are the condensed abelian groups), identifies the additive right adjoint of trivial inflation with this invariants functor, and [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] identifies trivial inflation with the inverse image $p_G^{-1}$ under the action-site presentation of step 2. Consequently $E p_s^*$ is canonically trivial inflation: both are left adjoint to the just-identified functor, and the unit/counit composites give inverse comparisons by the triangle identities. The descent equalizer above is computed for sheaves of sets, so the same adjoint-uniqueness argument identifies the set-valued inverse images $Ep_s^{-1}$ and $p_G^{-1}$; these are inverse images of geometric morphisms, hence preserve finite products, and the comparison therefore carries the ring operations of $R_s=p_s^{-1}R$ to those of $p_G^{-1}R$, the ring $R_G=p_G^{-1}R$ of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], which on the action site is $U\mapsto R(U)$ with restrictions $f^*$ by [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. In particular $E(R_s)$ is $R$ with trivial $G$-action, naturally in condensed ring maps.

source.place: Example 4.1.10; sheaf equalizer on the free cover of a trivial object

proof.text: The coefficient identification of step 3 makes $E$ a ringed-topos equivalence. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] it gives an exact additive module equivalence of $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}$ with modules over the trivially acted ring on the action site $C_G$ of step 2 and its termwise derived equivalence, preserving K-injectives. By [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], for the site of profinite sets (which has finite limits), the group sheaf $\underline G$ and the ring $R$, these are the $\underline G$-equivariant $R$-module sheaves, with the same section modules and restriction $m\mapsto a\cdot f^*m$ along $(f,a)$. Internal modules may be read as section-ring module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; this equivalence preserves their sections and restrictions identically, so the equivariant module sheaves are exactly the objects of $\mathcal A_G(R)$ in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. This defines the exact additive equivalence $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\simeq\mathcal A_G(R)$. We therefore retain the concrete normalization $(E_RN)(P)=N(\bar s[P])$, including its sectionwise $R$-action. Coefficient restriction commutes with $E_R$ by this formula: it changes only how $R(P)$ acts, via $R(P)\to R'(P)$, and leaves every section, restriction, and action map unchanged.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary internal-module transport through the field-site equivalence

proof.text: The functor $a_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] evaluates by $a_*M(V)=M(X\times_sV)$ on underlying sections by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]. Consequently $E_Ra_*M(P)=\Gamma(X^s[P],M|_{X^s[P]})$, with the action coming from the same right translations. This is the stated equivariant geometric section functor, now denoted $F_R$. Here $X\times_s\bar s[P]=X^s[P]$ by the natural test-object construction of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor], and the equality includes restriction and scalar actions. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] with $H=1$ to obtain that $\mathcal A_G(R)$ and $\mathcal M_R=\mathcal A_1(R)$ are Grothendieck abelian and that trivial inflation is exact, with the specified invariants right adjoint $\Gamma_G$. The ringed-site Grothendieck theorem applies to $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}$ after the section-ring equivalence in step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), identify the underived geometric section functor and its actual coefficient categories

proof.text: Evaluation at $*$ is exact on condensed abelian sheaves. It preserves kernels since kernels are sectionwise. For an epimorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] supplies local lifts of a section over $*$. A finite jointly surjective cover of $*$ has a nonempty member $P$; choosing $x\in P$ gives a section $*\to P$, and restricting the lift along it gives a global lift. Thus evaluation preserves epimorphisms. The section-ring equivalence of step 4 identifies the underlying abelian sheaves of internal modules. Their forgetful functor preserves finite limits and colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-left-exact, lem-sfb-modobj-forget-right-exact], so evaluation followed by forgetting scalars is exact on internal modules as asserted. The hypotheses on the tensor and on right exactness of $R\otimes-$ hold by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], which states these tensor functors are left adjoints.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, exact evaluation on an extremally disconnected profinite set; direct proof for the singleton

proof.text: Every complex in the three Grothendieck module categories of step 5 has a K-injective resolution, and ordinary total right derived functors exist by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. In particular this constructs $\mathcal K_R=\mathbf RF_R$ and $R\Gamma_G$ on all unbounded complexes. The left adjoint of $F_R=E_Ra_*$ is $a^*E_R^{-1}$. It is exact: $E_R^{-1}$ is exact, and [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] applies to every commutative condensed $R$, not just admissible coefficient rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $F_R$ carries K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. The same lemma applies to $\Gamma_G$, whose left adjoint is the exact trivial inflation of step 5. No boundedness or bound on group cohomology occurs here.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; unbounded resolutions as in the cited derived-category node

proof.text: For an $R_X$-module $M$, the equalizer of step 3 at $P=*$, applied to $a_*M$, gives the natural underived isomorphism $\gamma_M:\Gamma(X,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_*\Gamma_G F_RM$. It is the restriction of a section to $X^s$, with codomain the invariant sections; its inverse is the unique sheaf gluing. Choose a K-injective resolution $M\to I$. By step 7, $F_RI$ is already K-injective, so $R\Gamma_G(\mathcal K_RM)$ is represented by $\Gamma_GF_RI$. By step 6, $\operatorname{ev}_*$ needs no further derivation. The chain isomorphism $\gamma_I:\Gamma(X,I)\to\operatorname{ev}_*\Gamma_GF_RI$ therefore defines $\delta_{R,M}$. This proves the stated isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, rather than just a collection of cohomology isomorphisms. Derived naturality follows also from [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] applied to $a^*E_R^{-1}$ and trivial inflation: its K-injective formula is precisely this termwise comparison. The remaining exact evaluation preserves that formula.

source.place: Paragraph (3), derive the actual section/invariants comparison on one common unbounded K-injective representative

proof.text: For coefficient compatibility use actual ringed-topos morphisms. The functor $F_R$ is the direct image of the structure morphism $a$ followed by the ringed equivalence $E_R$; $\Gamma_G$ is the direct image of the action-topos morphism $p_G$ in [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Evaluation and forgetting scalars is the direct image from the condensed topos to the one-point topos with structural map $\mathbf Z\to R(*)$. For $\varphi:R\to R'$, scalar restriction is direct image on the identity underlying topos. The squares involving $a$, $E$, $p_G$, and evaluation commute as ringed morphisms: on sections every path is the original restriction map with scalar action precomposed by $\varphi$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to these paths. It supplies canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal K_R\operatorname{Res}_X\cong\operatorname{Res}_G\mathcal K_{R'}$, $R\Gamma_G^R\operatorname{Res}_G\cong\operatorname{Res}\,R\Gamma_G^{R'}$, and the corresponding global-section comparison. The normalization in that node ensures these are the derived comparisons of the stated underived maps. This application includes nonflat $\varphi$; it makes no assertion that scalar restriction preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied also to identity underlying topoi for coefficient restriction

proof.text:
The two coefficient-compatible routes around the desired $\delta$ square are the two parenthesizations of this same composite ringed direct image: first scalar restriction and then $a,E,p_G,\operatorname{ev}_*$, or scalar restriction at their successive targets. The associativity and identity equations of [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] identify these routes, including the normalization of step 8, since both underived section maps are restriction to $X^s$ followed by inclusion of fixed sections. Explicitly, let $c_{\Gamma}:R\Gamma_R(X,\operatorname{Res}M')\to R\Gamma_{R'}(X,M')$ be the global coefficient comparison and let $c_{\mathrm{inv}}$ be the composite of step 9 on the invariant side. The equality is
$$c_{\mathrm{inv}}\circ\delta_{R,\operatorname{Res}M'}=\delta_{R',M'}\circ c_{\Gamma}.$$
For $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}M'$, precompose with $R\Gamma_R(f)$ and use naturality of step 8. This proves coefficient-and-input naturality for every derived morphism in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D6E; associativity for the commuting coefficient-change paths, with its cocycle supplied by the cited node

proof.text: The right derived functors are triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Equip them with their canonical shifts. The comparisons in steps 8-10 are compositions of the canonical derived adjunction comparisons, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] makes their units and counits commute with those shifts. Alternatively the map of step 8 on a shifted K-injective representative is literally $\gamma_{I[n]}=\gamma_I[n]$, including the signed differential; the exact evaluation has the same termwise shift. Naturality at the third arrow $C\to A[1]$ of a distinguished triangle, together with this shift identity, gives the required connecting square, and hence a morphism of distinguished triangles. If $G=1$, fixed sections are all sections; if $X$ is empty or $R=0$, every displayed section module is zero. None of these cases changes the argument. No underived bar or continuous-cochain computation was used.
